subject: CLASS-ID paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB1086: Rule: 'The INHERITS clause specifies the names of classes that are inherited by object-class-name-1 according to 9.3.9, Class inheritance.' (cite.py --check 11.3.4 -> OK 11.3.4 2)). 9.3.9 (cite.py --check 9.3.9 OK): the subclass has all methods and all data definitions; each factory object has its own copy of inherited data, distinct from the copy belonging to a factory object of an inherited class, initialized when the factory of the subclass is created; names of inherited data items are not visible in the inheriting class. VERIFIED at 2002, 2014 and 2023: the new golden pb1086_inherited_factory_data_is_distinct (BUMP twice on the base, once on the subclass: CNT=102 / CNT=101 from the spec); instance data per object and the subclass's own V redeclared as in the earlier probes; a subclass method naming the base's data is COBOL1639; method inheritance and virtual dispatch oo_inherit (GR-11.3.4-2 is one of its rules); a superclass of ANOTHER compilation group is inherited through the external repository (ExternalRepositoryClassImportTests.AnImportedClassInheritingAnImportedClass_ImportsTheWholeChain; the note's extbase/extderived probe now prints EXB-HELLO). The plural 'names of classes' (a multi-base INHERITS) is Annex A.4.10 item 1, an OPTIONAL item this implementation does not claim and refuses COBOL0849 (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 5 row A.4.10; kb/Work PB285 closes SR-11.3.3-7 and GR-11.3.4-4 on that decision), so it is a documented non-support, not a defect of this row. File-definition inheritance is not probed. Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (CLASS-ID is a COBOL-2002 introduction; --std 85 refuses the unit COBOL0900).
